responsibility: `rustc_resolve` is the compiler crate responsible for Rust name resolution: it builds the crate’s module and definition graph, resolves imports and macros, performs late lexical and path resolution after expansion, computes visibility information, and emits the diagnostics and lints that arise from these passes before later compiler stages consume the recorded results. The root `lib.rs` defines the central resolver state, scope/binding machinery, query integration, and the overall orchestration that connects all subpasses and stores their outputs. `def_collector.rs` first assigns local definitions (`DefId`s) to AST nodes and preserves parentage across expanded code so later expansion and resolution attach new code to the correct definition tree. `build_reduced_graph.rs` then constructs and incrementally extends the reduced module graph from parsed and macro-expanded fragments, creating early bindings for items, modules, traits, enums, variants, fields, and imports and registering outstanding macro invocations. `ident.rs` provides the core identifier and path lookup logic across module, prelude, macro, derive-helper, and lexical scopes, including hygiene, namespace, ambiguity, and privacy-aware lookup behavior that other resolution stages rely on. `imports.rs` resolves `use`, `extern crate`, glob, and macro-related imports, integrates them into the module graph, handles reexports and partial resolutions, and diagnoses illegal, unresolved, hidden, ambiguous, or redundant imports. `macros.rs` handles macro-specific resolution for expansion, including `macro_rules!` scopes, hygiene-aware macro lookup, bang/attribute macro resolution, derive helpers, accessibility checks, and macro-resolution errors. `late.rs` performs the post-expansion late-resolution walk over items, expressions, patterns, types, lifetimes, labels, and doc links, resolving remaining lexical bindings and paths, enforcing rib-based scope rules, and recording final resolution metadata needed by later phases; its `late` submodule `diagnostics` supplies the context-sensitive diagnostics for late failures such as unresolved or ambiguous paths, labels, lifetimes, and associated items, including targeted typo/import/elision/shadowing suggestions and fallback lifetime handling to reduce cascaded errors. At the crate-wide and early-resolution level, `diagnostics.rs` builds and emits user-facing diagnostics for import, macro, privacy, ambiguity, and other resolver failures, computes fix suggestions such as where and how to insert `use` items, and buffers resolver-related lints; the separate `diagnostics` module contributes shared diagnostic helpers and validation utilities such as ordinal-number formatting used to keep resolver messages consistent. `errors.rs` defines the structured diagnostic payload types used throughout the crate so all these passes can emit consistent typed errors, labels, notes, and suggestions. `effective_visibilities.rs` computes effective visibility across the resolved module graph, including through reexports, updating tables used by privacy checking and metadata emission and identifying publicly exported ambiguous reexports for lints. Finally, `check_unused.rs` uses the resolver’s recorded usage information to prepare and emit lints for unused or redundant imports, unused `extern crate`s, unnecessary qualifications, and related `macro_use`/privacy import cases. Together these components make `rustc_resolve` the compiler stage that turns expanded AST names into resolved definitions, scopes, imports, macros, and visibility facts, while producing the resolver diagnostics and lint information required for the rest of rustc.
